title: Hadith Knowledge
description: General User → Mid. Familiar hadith knowledge, broader basics and short everyday applications. Covers well-known collections, responsible transmission and interpretation, and accessible Prophetic teachings. All questions are Mid level; specialist grading rules and reference-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires more understanding and simple connections than Beginner, without specialist study. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked hadith texts and publisher introductions checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Who compiled Sahih al-Bukhari?

options.text: Imam al-Bukhari
Imam Muslim
Imam al-Nawawi
Imam al-Tirmidhi

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari.

questions.question: Who compiled Sahih Muslim?

options.text: Imam al-Bukhari
Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
Imam Malik
Imam al-Nawawi

questions.explanation: Sahih Muslim was compiled by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj.

questions.question: Which two collections are commonly called the Two Sahihs?

options.text: Sunan Abi Dawud and Al-Muwatta
Riyad as-Salihin and Al-Adab al-Mufrad
Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim
The Quran and Sahih al-Bukhari

questions.explanation: The term refers to the collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim.

questions.question: What is a chain of narration in hadith study?

options.text: The order of chapters in the Quran
The numbering of pages in a printed book
A list of places where a book was sold
The sequence of people through whom a report was transmitted

questions.explanation: Studying transmission includes examining who conveyed a report.

questions.question: In the report beginning with an address to 'My servants,' whom does the Prophet quote as forbidding oppression?

options.text: Allah
Abu Dharr
A ruler of Madinah
The narrator's teacher

questions.explanation: The Prophet relates Allah's declaration that oppression is forbidden among His servants.

questions.question: Who was the visitor later identified as in the hadith about Islam, iman and ihsan?

options.text: Mikail
Jibril
A ruler from Yemen
An unknown merchant

questions.explanation: The Prophet explained that Jibril had come to teach the people their religion.

questions.question: What teaching method is prominent in the hadith of Jibril?

options.text: A competition over obscure dates
A lesson limited to trade prices
Questions and answers about foundational matters
A debate about family wealth

questions.explanation: The report teaches foundational matters through a sequence of questions and answers.

questions.question: What habit is warned against in the hadith about repeating everything one hears?

options.text: Asking for a reliable source
Admitting that one does not know
Correcting a mistaken report
Passing reports on without care or checking

questions.explanation: The warning encourages care rather than indiscriminate transmission.

questions.question: What broad teaching does the hadith give about acts of goodness?

options.text: Every act of goodness can be charity
Only donations above a fixed amount can be charity
Only public acts can have value
Helpful actions are unrelated to charity

questions.explanation: The hadith broadens our understanding of charity beyond financial giving alone.

questions.question: What encouragement is given to someone who guides another person to good?

options.text: Ownership of the other person's possessions
A reward similar to that of the person doing the good
Permission to claim every deed as their own
A guarantee of becoming famous

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages helping others find opportunities for good.

questions.question: What is true richness identified with in this hadith?

options.text: The largest number of possessions
Always having more than one's neighbors
Contentment of the soul
Being praised for expensive purchases

questions.explanation: The Prophet distinguished inner sufficiency from merely owning many things.

questions.question: What image describes believers in their mutual love and compassion?

options.text: Separate islands with no concern for one another
Competitors who benefit from each other's pain
A market judged only by profit
One body affected when a part suffers

questions.explanation: The image emphasizes shared concern and responsiveness to suffering.

questions.question: What image illustrates believers strengthening one another?

options.text: Parts of a building supporting each other
People trying to stand without any support
Rivals dismantling a shared wall
Travelers hiding every useful resource

questions.explanation: The Prophet used the image of a building and interlaced his fingers to illustrate mutual support.

questions.question: What conduct is linked with blessing in buying and selling?

options.text: Hiding defects behind attractive descriptions
Truthfulness and disclosure
Using pressure to prevent questions
Making claims known to be false

questions.explanation: The report links honest explanation with blessing and warns against concealment and lies.

questions.question: What did the Prophet object to when he found wet food hidden within a pile for sale?

options.text: Showing the food honestly
Allowing buyers to see the condition
Concealing its condition from buyers
Explaining how the food became wet

questions.explanation: The report condemns deception through hiding a problem buyers should be able to see.

questions.question: Which three sources of continuing benefit are mentioned after a person's death?

options.text: Fame, family rank and expensive possessions
Private savings, public praise and physical strength
A job title, travel records and social influence
Ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge and a righteous child who prays for them

questions.explanation: The hadith names these three ways benefit can continue after death.

questions.question: Which prophet is mentioned as eating from the earnings of his own work?

options.text: Dawud (David)
Yunus (Jonah)
Yahya (John)
Zakariyya (Zechariah)

questions.explanation: The Prophet praised earning through one's own work and mentioned Dawud as an example.

questions.question: Which quality is praised in the report about repaying a borrowed camel?

options.text: Using status to avoid repayment
Being good in repaying what one owes
Making the lender feel ashamed for asking
Denying the debt when repayment is possible

questions.explanation: The Prophet gave the lender his due generously and praised good repayment.

questions.question: What conduct does the hadith warn against when only three people are together?

options.text: Speaking so all three can take part
Welcoming the third person into the discussion
Two holding a private conversation that excludes the third
Waiting for a more suitable time for private matters

questions.explanation: The report gives concern for the excluded person's feelings as the reason.

questions.question: What practice concerning gifts did Aishah report about the Prophet?

options.text: He required every ordinary gift to be expensive
He treated every gift as permission for favoritism
He mocked those who offered simple gifts
He accepted gifts and gave something in return

questions.explanation: The report describes accepting gifts and responding with a gift in return.

questions.question: Does appearing in a hadith collection automatically establish every report's authenticity?

options.text: No, collections have different inclusion criteria
Yes, every collection contains only authentic reports
Yes, a printed page alone settles authenticity
Only a decorative cover is needed

questions.explanation: A report's status needs reliable assessment; inclusion alone is not enough.

questions.question: Why should an untrained reader avoid deciding a complex ruling from one isolated translated report?

options.text: Translation makes every legal question simple
Scholarly interpretation considers relevant evidence and context
One sentence always cancels all other evidence
Personal confidence replaces learning

questions.explanation: A report is not a complete ruling by itself; qualified interpretation matters.

questions.question: When explaining a hadith in your own words, what distinction should remain clear?

options.text: Every personal comment becomes part of the hadith
A useful explanation needs no connection to the report
Your explanation is not the Prophet's exact wording
Any inspiring sentence may be attributed to the Prophet

questions.explanation: Careful attribution includes distinguishing a report from our explanation of it.

questions.question: What does encouragement to convey even a little teaching require of the person sharing it?

options.text: Guess freely whenever knowledge is incomplete
Treat popularity as proof of accuracy
Add dramatic details to increase interest
Convey what is reliably known without inventing additions

questions.explanation: The same report that encourages conveying teaching also warns against lying about the Prophet.

questions.question: Does an attractive message make deliberate false attribution to the Prophet acceptable?

options.text: No, deliberate false attribution remains a grave wrong
Yes, if enough people enjoy it
Yes, if it produces more followers
Yes, whenever it mentions a good deed

questions.explanation: A claim should not be falsely put in the Prophet's name, even for a seemingly beneficial aim.

questions.question: What central obligation follows from the divine declaration against oppression in this report?

options.text: Assume power makes every action lawful
Avoid wronging other people
Treat another person's rights as irrelevant
Excuse harm whenever it brings advantage

questions.explanation: The report presents oppression as forbidden among Allah's servants.

questions.question: Does the broad use of charity in hadith make financial ability the only way to do good?

options.text: Yes, only money creates value
Yes, people without wealth can offer no good
No, goodness includes nonfinancial acts
Only wealthy donors can help a community

questions.explanation: The teaching recognizes goodness beyond money while preserving the value of financial charity.

questions.question: Can helping someone find a way to do good itself be valuable?

options.text: No, only doing every task personally can matter
Only if the helper becomes famous
Only if the person helped pays a fee
Yes, directing someone to good is rewarded

questions.explanation: The report encourages connecting people with a beneficial opportunity.

questions.question: Does contentment mean every practical need should be ignored?

options.text: No, inner sufficiency is different from denying real needs
Yes, needing food proves a lack of faith
Yes, planning for basic needs is always wrong
Only refusing every form of work counts as contentment

questions.explanation: The hadith challenges equating richness with possessions; it does not abolish ordinary needs.

questions.question: What response to another believer's hardship fits the image of one body?

options.text: Indifference because the pain is not personal
Concern that leads to appropriate support
Enjoyment of another person's difficulty
A belief that only public suffering matters

questions.explanation: The image encourages genuine concern rather than emotional distance.

questions.question: What principle does the image of a supporting building teach?

options.text: Useful cooperation always weakens personal faith
Every member should undermine the others
Mutual support strengthens a community
No one should ever accept help

questions.explanation: Believers are encouraged to reinforce one another rather than work against each other.

questions.question: What danger is highlighted by the hadith about the truly bankrupt person?

options.text: Having little money is itself a sin
A religious appearance removes the rights of others
Personal popularity prevents accountability
Wronging others can consume the reward of one's good deeds

questions.explanation: The report warns about arriving with acts of worship while owing others for serious wrongs.

questions.question: Why does honest disclosure matter even when a sale might be harder to make?

options.text: A buyer's decision should not be secured through deception
Profit removes every duty of honesty
Concealment becomes acceptable when common
Only the seller's immediate gain matters

questions.explanation: The hadith links truthful disclosure with blessing and warns against lies and concealment.

questions.question: What lesson does the report of hidden wet food give beyond that particular sale?

options.text: Only that exact kind of food can involve deception
Do not mislead people by concealing a material problem
A problem is harmless if the customer does not notice
A good sales pitch makes every concealment acceptable

questions.explanation: The specific event illustrates a wider warning against cheating.

questions.question: Why can teaching useful knowledge have lasting value?

options.text: Only the teacher's name needs to remain famous
Every opinion becomes beneficial simply by being recorded
People may continue benefiting from it after the teacher's death
The number of files matters more than their usefulness

questions.explanation: The report specifically connects continued benefit with knowledge that people use beneficially.

questions.question: What attitude toward honest work fits the hadith praising one's own earnings?

options.text: Only high-status work deserves respect
Manual work is always beneath a religious person
Dependence is better merely because it looks prestigious
Respect for lawful effort rather than contempt for modest work

questions.explanation: The hadith honors earning through one's own effort and gives a prophet as an example.

questions.question: What does good repayment emphasize?

options.text: Respecting what another person is owed
Using excuses to deny an acknowledged debt
Making repayment depend on public praise
Treating borrowed property as permanently one's own

questions.explanation: The report praises fulfilling another person's right well.

questions.question: Why does the instruction about private talk among three people matter?

options.text: Every conversation must be publicly broadcast
Exclusion can cause sadness and suspicion
Private conversations are forbidden in every setting
Words never affect people's feelings

questions.explanation: The instruction considers the emotional effect of excluding the only other person present.

questions.question: What everyday value can be learned from the Prophet responding to gifts?

options.text: Turning every gift into a demand for special treatment
Judging kindness only by price
Appreciation expressed through kindness in return
Using a gift to humiliate its giver

questions.explanation: The report provides an example of thoughtful reciprocity, not a rule that every gift buys influence.

questions.question: Which two blessings does the hadith warn many people fail to use well?

options.text: Wealth and ancestry
Fame and a job title
Clothing and physical height
Health and free time

questions.explanation: The hadith invites awareness of opportunities that can be wasted while available.

questions.question: A message says you must forward every religious story you receive. Which hadith principle challenges this?

options.text: Do not repeat everything indiscriminately
Forwarding automatically establishes truth
A religious label removes the need for care
More shares make any story reliable

questions.explanation: The warning about narrating everything one hears applies to careless forwarding too.

questions.question: One translated line is being used to settle a complicated personal ruling. What is a responsible next step?

options.text: Assume a screenshot settles every case
Seek qualified explanation of the relevant evidence
Ignore context because the line is short
Decide solely by which answer sounds easiest

questions.explanation: A complex ruling needs appropriate interpretation, not an isolated excerpt.

questions.question: You know a short teaching reliably but cannot explain a related detail. What should you do?

options.text: Invent the detail so the explanation seems complete
Claim certainty because admitting limits looks weak
Share what you know accurately and acknowledge the limit
Attribute a friend's guess to the Prophet

questions.explanation: Conveying a little accurately is better than expanding it with invented claims.

questions.question: You can gain an advantage by denying another person's clear right. Which lesson from this report applies?

options.text: Winning makes the method irrelevant
Another person's weakness cancels their right
A private wrong cannot matter
Personal advantage does not make oppression acceptable

questions.explanation: The declaration against oppression applies to how we treat others, including when wrongdoing would benefit us.

questions.question: You cannot provide a needed service, but know a reliable person who can. Which response fits the hadith?

options.text: Connect the person with that useful help
Assume helping has no value unless you do everything
Withhold the information to preserve attention
Pretend you can provide what you cannot

questions.explanation: Guiding someone to a beneficial opportunity is itself encouraged.

questions.question: A community member cannot donate money but can do a useful task. How should that contribution be viewed?

options.text: As worthless because no money is involved
As a meaningful act of goodness
As valuable only if filmed
As something that must be refused

questions.explanation: The broad teaching about goodness recognizes sincere practical contribution.

questions.question: You feel unsuccessful only because someone owns more than you. Which reminder fits the hadith?

options.text: More possessions always prove greater worth
Contentment requires despising everyone with wealth
True richness is not measured by possessions alone
Only public luxury makes a life meaningful

questions.explanation: The hadith directs attention toward inner sufficiency rather than endless comparison.

questions.question: A family in your community faces hardship. Which action fits the image of believers as one body?

options.text: Treat their suffering as irrelevant because it is not yours
Use their hardship for entertainment
Demand attention before showing concern
Notice their difficulty and offer appropriate support

questions.explanation: The image of the body encourages care that responds to another's pain.

questions.question: A useful community project has several tasks. What reflects the image of a supporting building?

options.text: Coordinate contributions so people reinforce one another
Hide information so others fail
Treat every helper as a rival to defeat
Refuse all cooperation to appear independent

questions.explanation: The image encourages strengthening one another through useful cooperation.

questions.question: A known fault could reduce the price of an item you are selling. What should you do?

options.text: Hide it until the payment is complete
Describe the fault honestly before the buyer decides
Claim an inspection is unnecessary because you seem trustworthy
Use a misleading description to protect the price

questions.explanation: The teaching on truthful disclosure applies even when honesty may affect the sale.

questions.question: A seller displays the good layer while concealing damaged goods underneath. Which report directly challenges that conduct?

options.text: The report about accepting gifts
The report about health and free time
The report of wet food hidden inside a pile
The report about private talk among three people

questions.explanation: The Prophet objected to a hidden condition buyers should have been able to see.

questions.question: You want a learning resource to remain beneficial after your death. What should take priority?

options.text: Only the prominence of your name
The largest possible number of unverified claims
Making it impossible for anyone to understand
Its accuracy and genuine benefit to learners

questions.explanation: Lasting educational benefit depends on useful knowledge, not merely leaving content behind.

questions.question: Someone mocks a person for earning through modest lawful work. Which reminder fits the hadith?

options.text: Honest effort deserves respect; Dawud earned through his own work
Only prestigious job titles deserve dignity
Lawful work becomes shameful when income is modest
Appearance matters more than the source of earnings

questions.explanation: The Prophetic example challenges contempt for earning honestly through one's own effort.

questions.question: You can repay an acknowledged debt that is now due. Which response fits the report on good repayment?

options.text: Delay only to show that they cannot pressure you
Give the person what is owed respectfully
Deny the debt because it was informal
Demand praise before returning their right

questions.explanation: Good repayment respects both the obligation and the person entitled to it.

questions.question: Only three of you are sitting together and you want a private discussion with one friend. What should you consider?

options.text: Whisper for a long time while pretending the third person does not exist
Assume the third person's feelings cannot matter
Avoid leaving the third person excluded; choose a suitable later setting
Use private talk to make them feel inferior

questions.explanation: The instruction warns against excluding the sole third person in a way that causes distress.

questions.question: You receive a thoughtful ordinary gift. Which response reflects the reported Prophetic example?

options.text: Treat the gift as permission to ignore fairness
Mock it if it is not expensive
Use it to demand a larger gift
Appreciate it and respond with suitable kindness

questions.explanation: The report describes accepting gifts and giving in return; it does not justify unfair favors or bribery.

questions.question: Someone says regular worship makes cheating and insulting people unimportant. Which hadith challenges this?

options.text: The hadith of the truly bankrupt person
The report about a seal on letters
The report about a pre-dawn meal
The report about repeating words to teach

questions.explanation: Acts of worship do not remove other people's rights; the hadith warns of accountability for harming them.

questions.question: You have a period of health and spare time. Which response applies the hadith's reminder?

options.text: Assume the opportunity must last forever
Use some of the opportunity for worthwhile activity
Treat every useful task as something to postpone indefinitely
Believe free time has value only when others notice

questions.explanation: The reminder encourages wise use of blessings while they are available.

questions.question: You want to alter a narration to make it more moving while still presenting it as the Prophet's words. What should you do?

options.text: Add invented words because the purpose seems good
Assume an emotional effect makes the wording authentic
Keep the attribution accurate and separate your own explanation
Change the report and supply a made-up reference

questions.explanation: A moving message does not justify deliberately putting invented words in the Prophet's name.

questions.question: A friend says relying on Allah means abandoning every useful effort. Which combination does this hadith teach?

options.text: Avoid action so that outcomes require no responsibility
Believe effort gives complete control over the future
Treat seeking help as a substitute for every duty
Pursue what benefits you and seek Allah's help

questions.explanation: The hadith combines beneficial effort with seeking Allah's help and warns against helpless resignation.
